summary: Lunar Outpost is a browser-based (html) mission trainer, made for young players ages 7-12, where you run a lunar outpost for 10 Moon days. Players choose a real landing site on a 3D Moon, with suggested sites including NASA Artemis III candidate regions and famous locations, filled with NASA data: LRO imagery and LOLA terrain, polar sunlight research papers, crater ice, and measured radiation. Every day brings real space weather from NASA's DONKI records (solar flares, coronal mass ejections, particle events, solar-wind streams), in addition to real eclipses, Moon phases, and meteor showers for that date. Players manage life support, power, and shielding, two crewmates, and repair failures. Built-in learning tools like a Learning Center that tells you how your actions impacted your simulation, a glossary for unknown words (e.g. DONKI), and an end-of-run report comparing the game to the real NASA record, which turn playing a game into learning skills. It matters because it teaches how real lunar missions work using the same data NASA uses, in a game a child can understand.
details:
Lunar Outpost is a browser-based, HTML, mission trainer. The player runs a three-person lunar outpost for 10 Moon day, starting by picking a landing site on a 3D Moon. Every site is scored from real NASA data like solar illumination, water ice, LOLA terrain roughness, and radiation amounts, and the choice will affect your game. Each day opens with a briefing from real NASA solar weather, plus the day's eclipse, Moon phase, or meteor shower. The player runs the life support, power, and shielding stations, picks one project a day, and repairs failures and gives orders to two crewmates. Survive all 10 days to win, and every game ends with a summary that shows how your actions resulted in winning or losing.

It turns NASA's data into something a child can play: players learn how real lunar missions work, like site selection, space weather, and supply timing, from real measurements. It is free, needs no install or account, and loads fast.

HTML canvas and JavaScript are used, no libraries. The data used from NASA are: NASA CCMC DONKI API, NASA OSDR, LRO/LOLA via the CGI Moon Kit, NASA GSFC eclipse catalogs, U.S. Naval Observatory phase tables, and the IMO meteor calendar.

The map is data, because where you choose your base site affects radiation, failures, and power generation for the game. Design priorities were making it not too complex (only three core resources for ages 7–12) and learning support (a word glossary for complicated words and a Learning Center that looks at one of your actions and describes how it helped or didn't help).
dataRefs: NASA LRO CGI Moon Kit and LOLA Elevation Data
projectRefs: U.S. Naval Observatory: Dates of Primary Phases of the Moon
